name: Polydactyly of a Biphalangeal Thumb and/or Hallux

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Polydactyly of Biphalangeal Thumb and/or Hallux

criteria.description: Presence of an extra digit on the thumb and/or hallux with biphalangeal morphology
Radiographic evidence showing biphalangeal structure of duplicated thumb and/or hallux
No associated syndromic features or other limb malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical identification of duplicated biphalangeal thumb and/or hallux confirmed by radiographic imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be performed to exclude syndromic polydactyly forms.

searchTerms: thumb with two phalanges instead of one
big toe with two bones duplicated
extra bone segments in big toe

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in duplicated digits
searchTerms: reduced movement range in duplicated fingers or toes

common.symptomName: Soft tissue syndactyly between duplicated digits

occasional.symptomName: Nail duplication or malformation on duplicated digits
searchTerms: extra or misshapen nails on duplicated digits
nail abnormalities on extra fingers or toes

occasional.symptomName: Mild localized swelling around duplicated digit
Callus formation due to abnormal digit positioning
searchTerms: skin hardening from abnormal finger position

occasional.symptomName: Mild functional impairment in grasp or gait

rare.symptomName: Associated carpal or tarsal bone anomalies

rare.notes: Rarely reported due to vascular anomalies
searchTerms: nerve and blood flow problems in extra finger
circulation and nerve issues in duplicated digit

imaging: Radiographs demonstrating biphalangeal duplicated thumb and/or hallux
X-rays showing absence of additional phalanges beyond biphalangeal duplication
genetic: Typically isolated sporadic or familial inheritance pattern
other: Physical examination revealing extra digit with biphalangeal bone structure

distinguishingFeatures: Triphalangeal duplicated thumb rather than biphalangeal
Extra digit located on ulnar or fibular side of hand or foot

redFlags: Presence of syndromic features such as craniofacial anomalies
Rapidly progressive swelling or infection in duplicated digit
